info.name: Enterprise API Security Auditor Agent (Meta Model API)
info.description:
Complete API collection for the **Enterprise API Security Auditor Agentic AI** project (Meta Global AI Developer Hackathon - *Build for Your World*).

Both agents reason on **Meta Model API**, model `muse-spark-1.3` (Muse Spark Open).

## Services
| Port | Service | Entry point |
|------|---------|-------------|
| 5000 | AI Agents (Audit + Remediate) | `backend/agents/init_auditor.py` |
| 5001 | Knowledge Ingestor (RAG) | `backend/rag/knowledge_ingestor.py` |
| 5002 | Redis Test Harness | `redis-test.py` |

## Setup
Paste your Meta key into `META_API_KEY` in `backend/.env`, then run
`python backend/scripts/verify_meta.py` to confirm the model is reachable.

## Recommended run order
1. **00 - Health Checks** - confirms the active LLM provider and model, Redis, and Kong.
2. **02 - Knowledge Ingestion (RAG)** - Create Index -> Ingest -> Search.
3. **03 - AI Agent: Audit** - Run Audit (saves `audit_report` as a collection variable).
4. **04 - AI Agent: Remediate** - Generate Remediation Plan (uses that variable).

Health responses report `dependencies.llm_provider` and `dependencies.llm_model`, so you can confirm at a glance that requests are served by Muse Spark Open.

item.name: 00 - Health Checks
item.description: Run these first. Each reports the effective configuration and which dependencies are degraded.

request.description:
Reports the effective configuration and every dependency.

**Confirms the hackathon requirement:** `dependencies.llm_provider` should be `meta` and `dependencies.llm_model` should be `muse-spark-1.3`. The test script asserts this.

Also reports `kong_mode`, `kong_services`, `policy_chunks` and `config.tls.system_trust_store`.

Returns 503 with a `problems` array when `META_API_KEY` is missing.

Returns 200 'ok' only when the embedding provider is configured, Redis is reachable WITH the RediSearch module, and the knowledge base directory exists. Otherwise 503 with a `problems` array naming each fault.
Reports the Redis host/port actually in use, which .env file was loaded, and whether the vector index exists.

item.name: 01 - Redis Test Harness (5002)
item.description: Standalone Redis checks that do not require the backend package. Useful for confirming connectivity before touching the RAG pipeline.

request.description: All fields optional. `recreate: true` drops and rebuilds the index while keeping the documents. Returns 201 when created, 200 when it already existed.

Stores an arbitrary text/embedding pair as a Redis hash under `embedding:<uuid>`.

NOTE: this writes a JSON blob, not a FLOAT32 vector, so documents added here are NOT returned by KNN search. It verifies connectivity and key layout only. Use `02 - Knowledge Ingestion` for real vectors.

query.description: Cap the number of documents returned
true decodes the float32 vector into 1536 numbers per chunk - large payload

request.description:
Lists every `embedding:*` key via SCAN (not FT.SEARCH, so there is no 10-document default cap).

Handles both document shapes that share the prefix:
- docs from `/redis/add_embedding`, whose `embedding` field is a JSON blob
- docs from the knowledge ingestor, whose `vector` field is packed FLOAT32 bytes

`vector_dimensions` is derived from the byte length (4 bytes per float32), so a value of 0 means the document has no real vector and will NOT be returned by KNN search.

The connection uses decode_responses=False deliberately: float32 vector bytes are not valid UTF-8, and decoding them raises "'utf-8' codec can't decode byte ...".
DESTRUCTIVE - removes every embedding, including the ingested policy corpus. Re-run the knowledge ingestion afterwards.

item.name: 02 - Knowledge Ingestion / RAG (5001)
item.description: The retrieval-augmented generation pipeline. Run Create Index -> Ingest -> Search in order.

request.description:
Creates the RediSearch index (`content`, `text`, `source` text fields; `vector` FLAT/FLOAT32/COSINE; `metadata` tag) over the `embedding:` key prefix.

Optional body: `index_name`, `prefix`, `vector_dimensions`, `recreate`. Ingestion calls this automatically, so it is only needed for explicit rebuilds.

Chunks every policy file in `backend/knowledge_base/`, embeds each chunk and stores it in Redis.

Body (optional):
- `reset` (bool) - delete existing chunks first, avoiding duplicates on re-ingest
- `knowledge_dir` (string) - override the source directory

The `knowledge_base/ALL/` subdirectory is skipped deliberately: it duplicates the top-level policy files verbatim and would double every chunk.

Cosine KNN search over the policy corpus - this is the request that proves RAG works.

Returns each hit with `source` (origin file), `score` (similarity, higher is better) and the chunk `content`. The audit agent issues the same query internally to ground its verdicts.

Try also: `rate limiting thresholds`, `GDPR data privacy requirements`, `input validation rules`.

query.description: Cap the number of chunks returned
true returns all 1536 raw floats per chunk - large payload

request.description: Inventory of stored chunks with their source file and metadata. Leave `include_vector=false` unless you specifically need the raw float arrays.
Index name, document count, stored chunk count, vector dimensions, and whether the RediSearch module is present.
DESTRUCTIVE - clears the policy corpus. The index definition is left in place, so a re-ingest does not need to recreate it.

item.name: 03 - AI Agent: Audit (5000)
item.description: The Audit Agent: Perceive (Kong) -> Retrieve (RAG) -> Reason (LLM) -> Plan -> Act.

request.description:
The service/plugin inventory the audit will run against.

Built from three Kong requests (services, routes, plugins) joined in memory, so the cost does not grow with the number of services.

`service_plugins` is the *effective* plugin set: plugins bound directly to the service, plugins bound to any of its routes, and gateway-wide plugins. Most Konnect estates bind plugins at the route level, so without the route rollup a service would look completely unprotected.

`source` is `kong_konnect` / `kong_onprem` when live, or `cached_file` with a `warning` when the Admin API is unreachable.

Runs the full audit graph against every service on the Kong control plane.

Body (all optional):
- `selected_standards` - standards in scope; defaults to ["All Security Standards"]
- `service_names` - audit only these services (see the next request)
- `top_k` - policy chunks retrieved per service (default 4)
- `kong_data` - inventory override; skips the Kong Admin API entirely

Cost scales with the estate: one LLM call per service. Measured against a Konnect control plane with 8 services this takes ~57s. Use `service_names` to narrow it during development.

Each audited service carries `policy_sources`, naming the policy files that grounded the verdict. `kong_source` reports provenance - `kong_konnect`, `kong_onprem`, `request` or `cached_file`.

The test script saves the report into the `audit_report` collection variable.

Audits an inventory supplied inline, bypassing the Kong Admin API. Use this to demo the agent when the Kong gateway is unreachable, or to test specific plugin combinations.

`PublicDocsService` has no plugins at all and should come back non-compliant across the board - a good smoke test that the reasoning step is genuinely evaluating the input.

Audits only the named Kong services. Names are matched case-insensitively against the service name in Kong.

This is the fast path for iterating: a full 8-service audit costs 8 LLM calls, while two services cost two (~17s measured).

Run `Kong Service Inventory` first to see the available service names.
Replays the most recent report from `backend/artifacts/langgraph_audit_report.json` without re-running the LLM. Returns 404 if no audit has run yet.

item.name: 04 - AI Agent: Remediate (5000)
item.description: The Remediation Agent: Perceive (findings) -> Retrieve (RAG) -> Reason (LLM) -> Plan (severity sort) -> Act.

request.description:
Turns non-compliant findings into an actionable plan. Returns a JSON array sorted Critical first, each item carrying serviceName, policyName, issue, missingPlugin, recommendedAction, severity, owner, estimatedEffort, impact and securityStandardReference.

Findings are sent to the model in batches of `REMEDIATION_BATCH_SIZE` (default 5). A single call for all findings grows with the estate and silently truncates past the token cap, which produces invalid JSON and loses the whole plan. If a batch still fails, it is retried one finding at a time so a single bad response cannot discard the group.

`{{audit_report}}` is populated by the Run Security Audit request.

exec: d.forEach(i => console.log('[' + i.severity + ']', i.serviceName, '-', i.policyName, '->', i.missingPlugin));

query.description: Wrap the array in an object with summary, findings_count and error detail

request.description:
With an empty body the agent falls back to the last audit report on disk, so remediation can be demoed standalone.

`envelope=true` returns `{remediation_plan, summary, findings_count, note, error}` instead of a bare array - more useful for debugging. The dashboard uses the bare-array form.
Replays the most recent plan from `backend/artifacts/langgraph_remediation_plan.json` without re-running the LLM.

item.name: 05 - Meta Model API (direct)
item.description:
Calls **Meta Model API directly**, bypassing this project entirely.

Model is driven by the `{{meta_model}}` collection variable (currently `muse-spark-1.3`).

### Models available to this key
Confirmed via `GET /v1/models`:
- **Chat / reasoning:** `muse-spark-1.3`, `muse-spark-1.3-contributor`, `muse-spark-1.2`, `muse-spark-1.2-contributor`, `muse-spark-1.1`
- Other modalities: `muse-wonder-1.0`, `muse-image-1.0`, `muse-voice-transcribe-1.0`, `sam-3.1`

`muse-spark-open` is **not** served by the Model API - it is an open-weights model intended to be self-hosted, so `meta-models/muse-spark-open-1026` returns `model_not_found`.

**If a response body starts with `<`** (an HTML page from Zscaler, Netskope or similar), the request was blocked before leaving your network. The key is fine, Meta never saw the request, and dashboard usage stays at 0.

request.description: 200 = key valid. 401 = key invalid or expired. HTML body = proxy block, not an auth problem.

exec: console.log('PROXY BLOCK - the request never reached Meta.');
pm.test('reached Meta (not a proxy block)', function () {
pm.expect.fail('An HTML page was returned by a network proxy, not Meta. '
+ 'Your key is fine; the request was blocked before leaving the network. '
+ 'No usage will appear on the Meta dashboard. Try a phone hotspot.');
